scope: P9 current-owned guild/group/P2P camera capture, live settings and preview retirement
behavior: A shared exact LocalParticipant camera owner replaces raw SDK camera toggling/device restart in guild and group calls. Video-only raw capture stays muted until a guarded publication commit, with immutable auth/source/admission/generation fences and immediate known-pending source retirement.

Actual installed LocalVideoTrack is userProvided, so SDK automatic device-change and ended-camera handling do not reacquire the camera. SDK constructor asynchronously enables raw according to isMuted: the owner registers the raw resource immediately, awaits public mute before publication, then performs guarded unmute with a post-await check.

Selected camera, quality and FPS changes replace the active owned camera while running. Off stops hardware. Permission/ended/current silent-ended failures show errors and explicit retry; silent endings during deferred mute/publish/unmute cannot leave starting or active success. Retired generations do not report failure into later owners.

Group camera uses the same preferences, actual ready indicator and translated error/retry path; no capture or camera controls before encrypted admission. Logical call retirement closes current capture. Guild retained Retry is gated by exact error-status identity and current camera owner.

P2P initial accepted video acquisition is retained. A per-call/PC/localStream/auth camera owner adopts that source, switches device/quality/FPS live, stops hardware when off, and uses operation generations so stale permission/finally work cannot clear later pending state. Ringing/ended calls cannot acquire camera.

P2P camera updates during a screen picker/share only update the local camera source, preserving the screen sender; screen start is refused while camera replacement is pending. This depends on the paired screen-quality slice and is committed as a reviewed union.
Preview remains explicit video-only, stops/invalidates on account retirement, drops late permission results, and never marks an already-ended return active.

Camera, screen replacement/restoration and screen encoder parameter mutations share one exact-RTCRtpSender queue. Camera rechecks valid ownership and non-sharing inside that queue; deferred restore/new-camera/new-share regressions prove no older restore or camera can overwrite the later screen owner. Current camera sender is rediscovered after camera was created while sharing.
